design_languages.name: Editorial Signal
design_languages.intent: A sharp product/editorial presentation language built around one visible protagonist, asymmetric evidence, restrained structural marks, and rhythmic contrast rather than repeated cards.
forbidden_aesthetics: four identical rounded cards as default proof layout

whitespace.rule: Whitespace is reserved around the visual protagonist before secondary content is placed; it is not leftover space after packing.

geometry.container_policy: use containers only when grouping is semantically meaningful

identity_anchors.description: A thin signal-colored path with one emphasized node, used only when a real sequence, dependency, or destination exists.
The strongest quantified conclusion sits directly in open space at large scale rather than inside a generic KPI container.
A high-contrast field may create a proof or terminal-action peak against a light canvas; it is semantic grouping and deck rhythm, not decoration.
A tiny optional edge marker may provide deck navigation without competing with title or source.

density_rules.low: One dominant idea, one support cluster maximum, large protected whitespace.
density_rules.medium: One protagonist plus two to five differentiated support objects; support may share a zone but should not normalize into identical tiles by default.
density_rules.high: Remove decoration, merge semantically related support, and change composition before reducing title/hero hierarchy. If still overloaded, fail and request content reduction.

variation_rules: Alternate protagonist anchoring across adjacent slides when semantics permit.
Vary open-canvas, split-field, edge-anchored, and bounded-product compositions while preserving typography and identity anchors.
Use high-contrast proof fields as rhythm punctuation, not as the default background.
Metric evidence may be hero-number, annotated comparison, scale, or support cluster; do not normalize all metrics into cards.
anti_repetition_rules: Never repeat the same archetype plus variation signature on adjacent slides unless explicitly marked as an intentional sequence.
Do not repeat the same protagonist position on three consecutive slides without an intentional-sequence marker.
Do not use the signal_path anchor on every slide.
Do not place every visual inside a rounded rectangle.
Do not use more than one major dark proof field on adjacent slides.
Do not render all supporting facts with identical size and contrast.
